questions.solution_html:
• Dietary modification for the elderly means adapting food quantity, texture and nutrient composition to
  • age-related changes, health conditions and chewing, swallowing or digestion difficulties.

questions.question: Explain how RDA serves as a guide in planning diets for healthy individuals.
questions.solution_html:
• A reference for daily nutrient intake. Estimate nutrient needs while planning balanced meals. Selection
  • and quantity of foods to meet nutrient requirements. • It helps assess whether a planned diet is likely to
  • be adequate for most healthy individuals. • It is used with dietary guidelines, food habits, activity
  • affordability and individual variation; it is not a diagnostic tool for an individual.
  • Scheme: (1 mark) for each of the five key points.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the major food and nutritional requirements of adults.
questions.solution_html:
• Energy needs should match age, sex, body size and physical activity to maintain healthy body weight.
  • Include cereals/millets or other whole grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits, and suitable protein foods.
  • Provide adequate high-quality protein for maintenance and tissue repair. Ensure adequate vitamins and
  • minerals, especially calcium, iron and other nutrients according to individual needs. Include healthy fats
  • dietary fibre and sufficient water; limit excess salt, added sugar and saturated/trans fats.
  • Scheme: (1 mark) for each of the five key points.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how Reference Man and Reference Woman are used to understand / nutritional requirements.
questions.solution_html:
• requirements.
  • Reference Man and Reference Woman are standardised descriptions of healthy adults used as reference
  • models. Defined with age, body weight, health and activity level in the relevant national guidance.
  • Estimate energy and nutrient requirements for population groups. Calculation and presentation of
  • reference values such as recommended nutrient intakes. Guides, not exact requirements for every
  • person; individual needs vary with body size, activity and physiological state.
  • Scheme: (1 mark) for each of the five key points.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of nutrition during adolescent growth.
questions.solution_html:
• Adolescence involves rapid increases in height, weight and tissue development, increasing energy needs.
  • Protein supports growth and repair of body tissues. Calcium and vitamin D support bone growth and
  • peak bone mass. Iron needs rise, particularly after menstruation begins; iron-rich foods help prevent
  • deficiency. A varied balanced diet, supports learning, immunity and physical activity; limit nutrient-poor
  • foods.
  • Scheme: (1 mark) for each of the five key points.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the role of prolactin in lactation.
questions.solution_html:
• Prolactin is a hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary gland. During pregnancy, prolactin levels rise
  • and prepare the mammary glands for milk production. After delivery, the fall in oestrogen and
  • progesterone permits prolactin to support milk synthesis. Suckling stimulates prolactin release, helping
  • maintain milk production. Frequent and effective breastfeeding supports continued production; prolactin
  • produces milk.
  • Scheme: (1 mark) for each of the five key points.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the dietary management of pregnancy-induced hypertension.
questions.solution_html:
• Balanced diet with adequate energy and protein appropriate to maternal needs. Include vegetables
  • fruits, whole grains and suitable protein sources; avoid highly processed foods. Avoid excessive salt.
  • Maintain appropriate fluid. Regular antenatal monitoring.
  • Scheme: (1 mark) for each of the five key points.

questions.question: Explain the importance of school lunch in meeting nutritional requirements.
questions.solution_html:
• Share of the child’s daily energy and nutrient needs. A balanced meal can provide cereals
  • pulses/protein foods, vegetables and other locally available nutritious foods. Helps prevent hunger and
  • supports attention, learning and participation in school. Improve dietary diversity. Promotes healthy
  • food habits and equity; hygiene, safe water and appropriate portion sizes are essential.
  • Scheme: (1 mark) for each of the five key points.

questions.question: Explain how dietary guidelines and ICMR-RDA can be integrated in practical / balanced-diet planning.
questions.solution_html:
• planning.
  • Assess the individual’s age, sex, activity level, physiological status, health and food preferences. Use
  • ICMR-NIN dietary guidelines to select a varied pattern of foods. Use the relevant RDA values as
  • reference targets. ((5 marks))
  • Distribute foods across meals. Adjust portions and food choices. Limit excess salt, added sugar and
  • unhealthy fats; ensure adequate fibre and water. Review the plan and modify it; ((5 marks))
questions.final_answer: unhealthy fats; ensure adequate fibre and water. Review the plan and modify it; ()

questions.question: Describe the role and functions of the placenta during pregnancy.
questions.solution_html:
• The placenta is a temporary organ that develops in the uterus and connects the foetus to the mother
  • through the umbilical cord. ((2 marks)).
  • Transfers oxygen and nutrients from maternal to foetal circulation. Transfers carbon dioxide and
  • metabolic waste products from the foetus for removal by the maternal organs. Acts as an endocrine
  • organ, producing hormones such as hCG, progesterone, oestrogens and human placental lactogen to
  • support pregnancy. Provides selective protection and transfers maternal IgG antibodies, contributing to
  • passive immunity; it is not a complete barrier to pathogens or harmful substances. Anchors the
  • developing pregnancy through its attachment to the uterine wall and supports exchange between
  • maternal and foetal blood without normally mixing them directly.
  • Scheme: Definition : (2 marks), Role and function – (2 marks) each (Any 4)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the role of food habits, meal pattern and food preferences in planning / a preschool diet.
questions.solution_html:
• • Assess the child’s usual food habits, appetite, cultural practices, family diet and any food restrictions.
  • • Offer regular meals and planned nutritious snacks;
  • Provide small, age-appropriate portions. Offer a variety of foods from major food groups. Respect
  • preferences. Use suitable textures, colours and child-friendly. Maintain food hygiene and safety. Adjust
  • the plan to growth, activity, appetite and nutrient needs; monitor growth over time.
  • Scheme: Role of food habits: (5 marks), Meal Pattern and food preferences – (5 marks)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the protective and immunological factors present in human milk.
questions.solution_html:
• • Secretory IgA provides mucosal protection by helping prevent pathogens from attaching to and
  • entering the infant’s tissues.
  • Lactoferrin binds iron and can inhibit the growth of some harmful bacteria.
  • • Lysozyme damages bacterial cell walls and contributes to antimicrobial protection.
  • • Human milk oligosaccharides act as prebiotics and can prevent some pathogens from attaching to the
  • intestinal lining.
  • • Leukocytes and other immune components, including cytokines and protective proteins, contribute to
  • immune defence.
  • • These factors support development of the infant gut microbiota and reduce the risk or severity of some
  • infections, especially gastrointestinal infections.
  • • Colostrum is particularly concentrated in immune factors; human milk provides ongoing protection but
  • does not eliminate all infection risk.
  • Scheme: Any 5 factors – (2 marks) each
